# AP-BAG-001 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes the procedures for the handling of checked baggage by AeroPolicy Airport staff between the check-in belts, the baggage make-up area, and aircraft loading. It outlines the responsibilities of staff members and defines the standards for baggage handling to ensure safety, efficiency, and compliance with regulatory requirements. This policy applies to all baggage handlers, baggage duty supervisors, and ramp leads involved in the movement, sorting, and loading of checked baggage. It ensures that all baggage operations are conducted in a manner that protects the integrity of the cargo and the safety of personnel and passengers.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities  
The Baggage Handler is responsible for the safe and efficient movement of checked baggage between the check-in belts and the baggage make-up area. The Baggage Duty Supervisor oversees the operations of baggage handlers and ensures compliance with handling standards and procedures. The Ramp Lead is responsible for coordinating baggage loading onto aircraft and ensuring that all baggage is properly secured and documented. All staff must follow established protocols, communicate effectively, and report any issues or incidents promptly. Each role has specific duties that contribute to the seamless and secure handling of baggage throughout the airport.

## 3. Handling Standards  
All baggage must be handled with care to prevent damage, loss, or misrouting. Baggage handlers must ensure that all bags are properly tagged, sorted, and loaded in accordance with airline and airport regulations. Heavy bags must be handled using appropriate equipment to avoid injury or damage. Fragile items must be clearly marked and handled with extra care to prevent breakage. All baggage must be visually inspected for damage or abnormalities before being moved or loaded. Any anomalies must be reported immediately to the appropriate supervisor for further action. Proper labeling and documentation are essential to ensure accurate tracking and delivery of baggage.

## 4. Baggage Incident Escalation  
When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 10 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All baggage incidents, including but not limited to damage, delays, or missing items, must be documented and escalated through the appropriate channels. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for assessing the incident and determining the necessary corrective actions. Any incident that may affect flight operations or passenger safety must be reported to the Ramp Lead for immediate resolution. All staff must ensure that incidents are escalated in a timely and accurate manner to maintain operational integrity and passenger satisfaction.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage  
If a restricted item is found in a bag during baggage handling, the bag must not be further processed until it is approved or removed under the restricted-items approval procedure in AP-SEC-003. Baggage handlers must immediately notify the Baggage Duty Supervisor upon discovery of any restricted item. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for initiating the approval process or coordinating the removal of the restricted item in accordance with applicable regulations. All bags containing restricted items must be clearly marked and isolated to prevent unauthorized access. The handling of such items must be conducted in a manner that ensures compliance with security and safety protocols while minimizing disruption to baggage operations.

## 6. Records and Review  
All baggage incidents must be recorded in the incident log for review and analysis. The incident log must include details such as the date, time, location, nature of the incident, and actions taken. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for maintaining and updating the incident log. The policy must be reviewed annually to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. Any changes to the policy must be communicated to all relevant staff and implemented in accordance with established procedures. Regular reviews and audits will ensure that the policy remains aligned with regulatory requirements and operational standards. All staff must be familiar with the policy and its requirements to ensure consistent and compliant baggage handling practices.
